newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's gross f/x reserves rise in June - Bank. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's gross f/x reserves rise in June - Bank. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]

text.p: Lebanon's gross foreign exchange reserves rose to $4.779 billion in June, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin issued on Tuesday.
The Bank said its gross reserves in foreign currencies rose by $31.6 million (corrects from "rose by 31.6 percent") from $4.747 billion a month earlier and grew by 53 percent from June 1995.

The central bank did not give figures for the net foreign exchange reserves for the fifth consecutive month. They had increased by $130.4 million in January. They stood at $2.858 billion at the end of 1995.
Banking sources told Reuters they stood at $3.5 billion on August 15, 1996.
The Bank said foreign currency reserves rose in June "due to capital inflows, foreign exchange purchases by the Bank and porfolio shifts towards Lebanese pounds assets."
Gross reserves include commercial banks' foreign exchange deposits with the central bank.
